newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan lists condition to attend HK handover event.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan lists condition to attend HK handover event.

text.p: Taiwan's top mainland policy planner said on Friday the island would allow officials to attend ceremonies marking the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule -- but only if the officials were given due respect.

"Only when our officials are given proper treatment with dignity and respect shall we agree to send officials to attend the ceremonies," Chang King-yuh told reporters after taking part in a seminar in Taipei.

Chang, chairman of the cabinet's Mainland Affairs Council, was referring to arch-rival China's proposal to invite representatives from Taiwan to attend the ceremony scheduled to be held in the British colony at midnight on June 30.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said in Beijing on Thursday that China would invite Taiwan people to attend the ceremonies.

But he stressed that Taiwan residents invited to witness the end of London's 156 years of colonial reign in Hong Kong would have to approve of the territory's return to Beijing and accept the "one-China" principle.
Communist-ruled China has regarded Taiwan as a rebel province since 1949, when defeated Nationalist forces took refuge on the island at the end of a long civil war.

Beijing, which reserves the right to invade Taiwan if it ever declares formal independence, has repeatedly demanded the island's leaders accept the principle of "One China" and prove their intention to eventually reunify with the mainland.
Taiwan's news media has reported that China was likely to invite Koo Chen-fu, chairman of the quasi-official Straits Exchange Foundation, to the ceremonies.
Koo has said he had not yet received any invitation.

The foundation and its mainland counterpart, the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Strait, have been used by Beijing and Taipei as a way to negotiate without breaking their ban on direct official contacts.
Even such semi-official talks stalled in June 1995 after Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui enraged Beijing by making a landmark private visit to the United States, but tensions have eased recently.
